# v0.2 repeat statistics (generated by scripts/ci_stats.py)

- Events: **30**; runs: **90** (3 runs per event)
- Scores input: `data/repeat_v02/scores.jsonl` (sha256 562be6853fba6906)
- v0.1 baseline: `data/repeat_v02/scores_v01.jsonl`
- Statistical unit: event. Repeats estimate run-to-run noise; they are NOT independent samples.
- Scoring: hit = yes 1 / partial 0.5 / no 0, per run 0-3; hit rate = event-mean score / 3.

## Headline (the numbers quoted in README.md)

| Metric | Value | 95% CI / spread | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Top-3 risk hit rate** (event mean) | **82.2%** | 78.5-85.9% (t, df=29) | mean 2.47/3, n=30 events |
| Same, percentile bootstrap | 82.2% | 78.7-85.6% | 10000 resamples, seed 20261026, numpy |
| Paired diff vs v0.1 single run | -0.02/3 | ±0.18 | 30 events, paired |

## Variance and stability

| Metric | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Between-event SD | 0.30/3 | spread of difficulty across events |
| Within-event SD (mean) | 0.26/3 | same event, re-run: run-to-run noise |
| Within-event SD (median) | 0.24/3 | |
| Events identical in every run | 5/30 = 17% | same score all 3 runs |
| Events with within SD >= 0.5 | 2/30 = 7% | #21, #23 |
| Events at a perfect 3/3 in every run | 0/30 = 0% | Wilson 0-11% |
| Events at a perfect 3/3 at least once | 14/30 = 47% | headroom from reading a consensus of repeats |
| Runs scoring a perfect 3/3 | 21/90 = 23% | descriptive only (runs are correlated) |
| Early-warning quality | 78/100 | 75-81, event mean ± t |

## Scoring discipline (do not quote the headline without these)

1. 82.2% is an **event-mean graded score**, not a binary hit/miss rate. The binary framing on 30 events is roughly ±17pp; do not mix the two.
2. 90 runs are **not** 90 independent samples; the unit is 30 events.
3. The interval covers sampling and run randomness only. It does **not** include LLM-judge error or systematic bias from a 2-round simulation.
4. Only 5 of 30 events score identically across repeats: commit to a consistent level, never to 'the same conclusion every time'.
5. This is a rehearsal/backtest producing directional evidence, not a forecast.

> Reproduce: `python scripts/ci_stats.py --out data/repeat_v02`
